identity.title: Nuchal rigidity (neck stiffness on passive flexion)

technique.how: With the patient supine and relaxed, cup the occiput and passively flex the neck so the chin approaches the chest, then rotate side to side. Nuchal rigidity is present when flexion is resisted or painful while rotation remains relatively free; also ask the patient to touch chin to chest actively.
technique.prerequisites: No suspected cervical spine injury; patient calm enough to relax the neck muscles.
technique.contraindications: Suspected cervical spine trauma or instability.

interpretation.positive_finding: Meningeal irritation is possible but the sign does not discriminate in prospective cohorts (LR+ about 0.9-1.0 for CSF pleocytosis); sensitivity approached 100% only in the few patients with severe pleocytosis.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absent in 70-87% of patients with pleocytosis, so absence must not be used to exclude meningitis. The RCE reports that absence of all three of fever, neck stiffness and altered mental status is what effectively rules out meningitis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Cervical spondylosis, parkinsonism and voluntary guarding produce false positives; elderly, immunosuppressed and obtunded patients produce false negatives.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: modestly raises urgency for LP and empiric therapy; negative: no change, base the LP decision on fever, headache, AMS and host risk.

estimates.population: 297 adults with suspected meningitis evaluated before LP
estimates.reference_standard: CSF white cell count >=6/mL at lumbar puncture
estimates.quote: nuchal rigidity (sensitivity, 30%; LR(+), 0.94) did not accurately discriminate between patients with meningitis

estimates.population: 230 neurologically intact adult ED patients undergoing LP, AMS excluded
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.13/(1-0.80); LR- = (1-0.13)/0.80 from rounded abstract sens/spec
estimates.quote: the sensitivity of jolt accentuation was 21%, Kernig sign was 2%, Brudzinski sign was 2%, and nuchal rigidity was 13%

estimates.target_condition: Acute meningitis - absence of fever, neck stiffness AND altered mental status (composite)
estimates.population: Pooled adult meningitis studies in the RCE (10 studies)
estimates.quote: the absence of fever, neck stiffness, and altered mental status effectively eliminates meningitis (sensitivity, 99%-100% for the presence of 1 of these findings)

sources.citation: Thomas KE, Hasbun R, Jekel J, Quagliarello VJ. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis. Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52.
Nakao JH, Jafri FN, Shah K, Newman DH. Jolt accentuation of headache and other clinical signs: poor predictors of meningitis in adults. Am J Emerg Med 2014;32:24-28.
Attia J, Hatala R, Cook DJ, Wong JG. The rational clinical examination. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-181.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never use absent neck stiffness to defer LP or antibiotics; avoid passive flexion with possible cervical injury.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Fever with headache and AMS, purpura, or immunosuppression requires empiric antibiotics and LP irrespective of this sign.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Attia RCE notes the sign is inconsistently defined across studies; Thomas 2002 abstract reports the sign had value only in 4 patients with >=1000 WBC/mL (sensitivity 100%).

extraction_notes: Thomas 2002 specificity and LR- not in abstract and full text not OA, so left null. The RCE composite (sens 0.99-1.00 recorded as 0.99, its lower bound) is for absence of all three findings, not nuchal rigidity alone; specificity not reported in the abstract. Nakao LR computed from rounded percentages. PMIDs confirmed.
